name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,738

clue.text: Lookin' for Queen in horse publication

indicators.note: putting one thing 'for' another means swapping it into that other's place

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen
gazing means looking, with the final G dropped just as the clue drops it

explanation.surface: Someone flicks through a horsey magazine hoping to spot the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Lookin'' warns that the replacement word is clipped, just as a speaker drops a final G. R standing for Regina is the usual crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is a periodical, a regular printed publication sold to readers.

clue.text: Area primarily encompassing Greece's Euboea and Naxos?

definitions.text: Area primarily encompassing Greece's Euboea and Naxos?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the leading letter of each word counts

blocks.note: the first letter
the first letter
the first letter
the first letter
the first letter
the first letter

explanation.surface: A geography question about a sea region taking in two Greek islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the initials of its six words spell the answer, and read straight it describes that very sea, which surrounds Euboea and Naxos.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aegean is the stretch of Mediterranean water between Greece and Turkey, holding many Greek islands.

clue.text: Can I tie Sid in knots for strict regime advocates?

indicators.note: something tied in knots is twisted out of its straight order

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they may tie up a man called Sid for the benefit of authoritarian types.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strict regime' suggests a political dictatorship, but the regime here is a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieticians are nutrition experts who prescribe controlled eating plans, a strict regime of food.

clue.text: Obsessive party news outlets impressed by criminal joker

indicators.note: something impressed by another is pressed into it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: a stan is slang for an obsessive fan
the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland
a con is a convict
the media are the outlets that carry news

explanation.surface: A fanatical political party uses its press to leave an imprint on a crooked prankster.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan, from the Eminem song, is modern slang for a superfan, and the Democratic Unionist Party is a Northern Ireland political party. 'Joker' is a comic, not a criminal, despite its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up comedian tells jokes to an audience for a living, so is a professional joker.

clue.text: Henry leaves curses for old partners

indicators.note: whatever leaves goes away, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
hexes are spells or curses

explanation.surface: A man named Henry walks out, leaving curses behind for his former partners.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a name, but it is the physics unit, abbreviated H; remove it from HEXES.
explanation.definitionFit: Exes are former spouses or lovers, people one used to be romantically attached to.

clue.text: Square cardinal is expected to give support to nationalist

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece sits underneath the one it holds up

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for nationalist
if one ought to do something, one is expected to

explanation.surface: A conservative churchman is duty-bound to back a nationalist cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square cardinal' reads as a stuffy prince of the Church, but it is a cardinal number that is also a perfect square: zero squared is zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Zero is a cardinal number, and as zero times zero it counts as a perfect square.

clue.text: Eastender's equally hirsute as person from the Caucasus

indicators.note: an East Ender speaks Cockney, which drops the H, so the words are said in that accent

blocks.note: equally is AS and hirsute is HAIRY, said in Cockney without its H

explanation.surface: A Londoner remarks that someone from the Caucasus is just as hairy.
explanation.walkthrough: East Enders are Cockney Londoners, famous for dropping the H at the start of words, so 'hairy' comes out as 'airy.
explanation.definitionFit: An Azeri is a native of Azerbaijan, a country lying in the Caucasus region.

clue.text: Perfect cowboy nickname: "Shot Bot Jake"

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or knocked out of shape

blocks.note: Tex, short for Texan, is a stock cowboy nickname
taken as written
jake is old slang for fine or all right

explanation.surface: A flawless Western nickname for a gunslinger: Shot Bot Jake.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted name looks like one invented cowboy, but it splits three ways: Shot works on Bot, and Jake is slang meaning satisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: A textbook example is a model one, done exactly by the rules, so ideal or perfect.

clue.text: Field glasses worn by bad researchers

indicators.note: whatever is worn goes around the wearer, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: bins is British slang for binoculars
food that has gone bad has gone off

explanation.surface: Poor scientists out in a field wearing binoculars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field glasses' is one unit meaning binoculars, called bins in British slang, not a field plus spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British slang for a scientist or technical expert engaged in research.

clue.text: Farewell broadcast of tennis lovers

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it widely, so these letters are strewn about

blocks.note: vale is Latin for goodbye
taken as written

explanation.surface: A televised goodbye to devoted fans of tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests TV, fitting the tennis picture, but it scatters the letters of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is a sweetheart chosen on 14 February, so valentines are romantic partners.

clue.text: Amusing chap detailed delicacy with poison

indicators.note: de-tailed means with the tail cut off, so each word loses its last letter

blocks.note: fun can mean amusing
a guy is a chap

explanation.surface: A funny man describes in detail a dish laced with poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' reads as 'explained fully', but split as de-tailed it means each word loses its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Fugu is Japanese pufferfish, a prized dish that is lethal if its toxic organs are not removed.

clue.text: Writer describes Particle Man's type of enhancements in 70s show

definitions.text: Man's type of enhancements in 70s show

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so one piece is drawn around the other

blocks.note: a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: An author writes about the gadgets of the superhero Particle Man in a 1970s TV series.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make 'Particle Man' look like a title, but Particle goes into the pen and 'Man' belongs to the definition, recalling The Six Million Dollar Man.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Six Million Dollar Man, the hero was rebuilt with bionic limbs, electromechanical body parts giving superhuman powers.

clue.text: Restless one who French epigraphist deserted

indicators.note: a deserted place has been emptied, so only the outside shell of the word is left

blocks.note: in French, one is UN and who is QUI
only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A fidgety person was abandoned by a French expert in inscriptions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks like the nationality of the epigraphist, but it translates the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unquiet is a literary word for uneasy or agitated, unable to settle, as a restless person is.

clue.text: Attributed words from a third of Rossi's band to rocking with Saint

indicators.note: a rocking object tips back and forth, so these letters are shaken out of order

blocks.note: Francis Rossi fronts Status Quo; split into three three-letter parts, the last is QUO
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lyrics credited to part of Francis Rossi's rock band, who are rocking alongside a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Status Quo are a long-running British rock band led by Francis Rossi; STATUS QUO has nine letters, so a third is three of them. 'Rocking' suits the band but works on TO plus SAINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Quotations are passages repeated from a source and credited to the original speaker or writer.

clue.text: Spice Girls canon remixed in Walker's place by Pavement

indicators.note: a remix reworks the parts of a track into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, fifteen letters

explanation.surface: The Spice Girls' catalogue is reworked with Scott Walker's role taken by the indie band Pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: Walker and Pavement look like musicians, matching the pop surface, but here a walker is a pedestrian and a pavement is a sidewalk. A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with push-button traffic lights.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelican crossing is a road crossing point next to the sidewalk where pedestrians stop traffic by pressing a button.

clue.text: Japanese island Okinawa's on a Jewish mosaic displayed occasionally

indicators.note: shown only now and then, so just some letters at a steady interval appear

blocks.note: every third letter, starting from the third

explanation.surface: An Okinawan island scene pictured in a Jewish mosaic, put on show from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Okinawa is a tempting island to write in, but it is only letter fodder; the answer is a different Japanese island.
explanation.definitionFit: Iwo Jima is a small volcanic island south of Tokyo, famous for its 1945 battle.

clue.text: Sensitive spot in North-East Denver undergoing quake

indicators.note: something going through an earthquake is shaken apart and rearranged

blocks.note: the compass abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vulnerable area in the north-east of Denver is hit by an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sensitive spot' sounds like a geological fault line, fitting the quake, but it is a part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve ending is the tip of a nerve fibre that senses touch or pain, a highly sensitive point.

clue.text: Dispersed items lost abroad amongst kinsfolk

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so these letters are spread into a new order
to be amongst others is to sit in the middle of them

blocks.note: taken as written
fam is slang for family

explanation.surface: Belongings scattered and lost overseas while travelling with relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' seems to mean overseas, but in its older sense of widely spread it rearranges LOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is wreckage and goods left floating after a ship is lost, scattered across the sea.

clue.text: Companion of castaway fellow freed a Yorkshireman's capital

indicators.note: a capital is a leading letter, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
to be rid of something is to be freed of it
taken as written
the first letter

explanation.surface: A shipwrecked man's companion freed a Yorkshireman's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' reads as money or a city, but it simply means the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Defoe's Robinson Crusoe, the stranded hero is joined by Man Friday, his loyal servant and friend.

clue.text: Home for 21 perhaps built by tracks on a Roman road

indicators.note: in an across entry, what comes on something else follows it

blocks.note: taken as written
via is Latin for road
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A dwelling built beside railway lines along an old Roman road.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 across is KIWI, which is also a bird, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviary is a large enclosure where captive birds, such as a kiwi, are kept.

clue.text: Tense TV panel show's elevated trial of wit

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters up turns them upside down

blocks.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a TV is a television set
QI is a BBC comedy quiz panel show; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A nervy TV panel show has grown into a highbrow battle of wits.
explanation.walkthrough: QI is a British TV quiz show hosted by Stephen Fry and later Sandi Toksvig. 'TV' is not an abbreviation to keep but a SET.
explanation.definitionFit: An IQ test measures intelligence, so it is a formal examination of one's mental sharpness.

clue.text: Islander's skis - two twigs, essentially

indicators.note: the essence of a thing is its core, so only the central letters count

blocks.note: the two central letters
the central letter
the central letter

explanation.surface: An island dweller's skis are basically just a pair of sticks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two twigs' looks like one phrase, but each of the three words gives up its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiwi is the everyday nickname for a New Zealander, a native of an island nation.

clue.text: "When Twiggy first modelled" - cryptic clue to a T?

blocks.note: first meaning: the model Twiggy became famous in 1966
second meaning: the letter at the centre of a word for a decade, read literally

explanation.surface: A quote describing Twiggy's modelling debut, followed by a note that it hints at a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: the middle of SIXTIES is its fourth letter, T. Twiggy was the famous 1960s London fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: Twiggy began modelling in 1966, halfway through that decade, and the centre of 'sixties' is its T.

clue.text: Ditch very small part in speech

indicators.note: in speech means spoken out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a mote is a tiny speck

explanation.surface: Advice to cut a tiny role in a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a verb meaning drop, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A moat is a deep water-filled trench dug around a castle for defence.

clue.text: Prince reviewed Open with an amateur

indicators.note: to review is to look back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a door that is ajar is open
the indefinite article
a ham is an amateur, as in a radio ham

explanation.surface: A royal golfer is written up playing in the Open with an amateur partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open is golf's major championship, and 'reviewed' sounds like press coverage; here open is AJAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja is an Indian king or great ruling prince of a princely state.

clue.text: Car (not a Sierra) seen in part of a religious calendar

indicators.note: not having something means it is left out

blocks.note: Nissan is a car maker
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A car that is not a Ford Sierra spotted during a religious festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sierra was a well-known Ford model, which suits the car, but it is only the radio code word for S.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisan is the first month of the Jewish religious year, in which Passover falls.
